messages:
Maya: heads-up, noticed a burst of small GPU pod evictions in eu-west1 this morning. lots of 0.25/0.5 GPU jobs getting reshuffled and leaving 'orphaned' shards on nodes.
Sergio: saw that too, eviction rate spiked ~03:12 UTC, correlates with a scheduling defrag job + AZ imbalance.
Maya: ops-bot alert pasted below, looks like the scheduler kept preferring a compacting policy and then failed to pack >1.0 GPU slices so pods got preempted.
ops-bot: ALERT: gpu-eviction-rate > 120/min in eu-west1-a for 10m. top reasons: affinity_fails, insufficient_local_gpus, fragment_compact_requeue.
Sergio: pasting kube-scheduler snapshot:```QueuedPod: gpu-request=0.5 nodeCandidates=6 reasons=[taint:gpu-scarce, affinity:cohort-mismatch] SchedulingCycle=4```
Dmitri: suspecting the 'compactness-entropy' heuristic we rolled out last week — it aggressively consolidates to reduce node count but doesn't respect micro-slot fragmentation, so small jobs get churned.
Leila: FYI this caused a transient latency increase for hosted API under small-batch workloads (p50 up ~40ms). also noticed cross-az network egress bumped when pods moved.
Maya: temporary mitigation idea: lower compactness weight and add a min-stable-window=300s for GPU allocations to avoid immediate re-eviction of small slices. can we do a quick canary?
Sergio: I can flip compactness weight -> 0.6 in eu-west1 canary pool now. will watch evictions and packing metrics. /who wants to approve short rollback window? @Dmitri @Leila
Dmitri: +1 to canary. also propose a defrag job that runs during 03:00-05:00 UTC doing "planned compaction": cordon low-util nodes and migrate full-gpu pods first, avoid messing with fractional slices.
Leila: agree, but we should add cost guardrail: avoid scaling down unless expected savings > 12h to justify migrations. otherwise cost/latency tradeoff bad.
Sergio: canary applied at 03:40 UTC. initial numbers: eviction-rate down 55% in the canary pool, but binpacking efficiency also dropped ~6% (more nodes used).
Maya: good trade for production stability. next steps: (1) ship min-stable-window + compactness tuning as short-term, (2) schedule planned compaction job that prefers whole-gpu consolidation, (3) add a scheduler metric "fractional-shard-orphans" and alert on >100/min.
Dmitri: I'll draft the planned compaction playbook and a safe rollout plan (drain windows, K8s PDB-aware migrations).
Leila: ping infra-cost with the numbers so finance can model the 6% node increase. ops-bot, mute noisy alerts for the canary channel for 2h. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Muting alert stream for canary pool for 2h per request from Sergio."
